final_method_items.signature: static tree create_expression_by_pieces (basic_block block, pre_expr expr, gimple_seq *stmts, tree type)
final_method_items.summary: Create an expression in pieces, so that we can handle very complex expressions that may be ANTIC, but not necessary GIMPLE. BLOCK is the basic block the expression will be inserted into, EXPR is the expression to insert (in value form) STMTS is a statement list to append the necessary insertions into. This function will die if we hit some value that shouldn't be ANTIC but is (IE there is no leader for it, or its components). The function returns NULL_TREE in case a different antic expression has to be inserted first. This function may also generate expressions that are themselves partially or fully redundant. Those that are will be either made fully redundant during the next iteration of insert (for partially redundant ones), or eliminated by eliminate (for fully redundant ones).

behavior_items: The real reproducer is the `small.c` program embedded in the report, not the leading backtrace text accidentally included in the `reproducer_code` field. It declares global variables `int a, b, d; unsigned c;` and defines `main` with a local `int f = 0;`.

At runtime, `while (a)` controls the whole loop. Because `a` is a zero-initialized global, a normal execution of the compiled program never enters the loop unless some external action changes `a`; this makes the test primarily a compiler-stress case rather than a meaningful runtime test.

Inside the loop, `unsigned g = c;` snapshots the global unsigned `c` into a local temporary. This gives later expressions two equivalent views of the same value: one directly as `c` and one through SSA name `g`, which is useful for value-numbering and PRE reasoning.

The `if (f) printf("0");` branch introduces control flow depending on `f`, where `f` is initially zero and later assigned from `c`. This creates a loop-carried SSA value and a conditional side-effecting call, so the loop body is not a single straight-line block after GIMPLE lowering.

The statement `~(c << 1);` computes a value but discards it. Since the expression has no side effects, it is dead code semantically. However, the bug is triggered specifically with `-fno-tree-dce` and `-fno-tree-dse`, so GCC is forced to carry this otherwise removable computation farther into optimization than usual.

The expression `b = ~-(a * d && 1) | g * -2 && a;` is the main stress point. It mixes arithmetic, bitwise, logical, precedence-sensitive parsing, and implicit boolean conversion in one assignment, producing several intermediate GIMPLE expressions that optimizers may try to reuse or partially hoist.

Because `&&` has lower precedence than `|`, the right-hand side parses as `((~-(a * d && 1)) | (g * -2)) && a`, not as `~-(a * d && 1) | ((g * -2) && a)`. So GCC must first build the bitwise-OR result, then convert that integer result to a truth value for the final logical-AND with `a`.

The subexpression `(a * d && 1)` is equivalent to testing whether `a * d` is nonzero. Since `&& 1` yields exactly `0` or `1`, applying unary minus gives `0` or `-1`, and bitwise complement `~` turns those into `-1` or `0` respectively. This is an unusual but valid way to synthesize a mask-like value from a boolean.

The subexpression `g * -2` on an unsigned `g` performs multiplication in unsigned arithmetic after the usual conversions, effectively yielding `-2u * g` modulo the unsigned type width. This can be recognized as a left-shift-like doubling with wraparound and then negation, but it remains an integer-valued expression whose bits feed the `|` operation.

After the bitwise OR, the logical `&& a` converts the left operand to boolean, short-circuits if it is zero, and otherwise yields whether `a` is nonzero. Therefore the assigned value of `b` is always either `0` or `1`, even though the left side of the `&&` is built from complex integer/bitwise operations.

The assignment `f = c;` at the end of the loop feeds the next iteration's `if (f)` condition. Since `f` is `int` and `c` is `unsigned`, the conversion may preserve or reinterpret the same bit pattern depending on width, but on common targets both are 32-bit and the resulting condition is simply whether `c` was nonzero.

Optimization-wise, the loop creates a classic setting for Partial Redundancy Elimination (PRE): repeated use of `a`, `c`, and expressions derived from them across control-flow edges, combined with a conditional call and a loop-carried variable. PRE may try to represent some computations as available expressions and insert them on predecessor edges.

The crash occurs during the GIMPLE `pre` pass (`tree-ssa-pre.cc`), specifically along `find_or_generate_expression -> create_expression_by_pieces -> insert_into_preds_of_block`. That means GCC is not merely simplifying an expression; it is attempting to synthesize or materialize an expression form in predecessor blocks as part of PRE insertion.

The immediate fault at `bmp_iter_set_init` suggests PRE is using an invalid or uninitialized bitmap while walking operand/value sets for one of these generated expressions. In practice, that points to corrupted internal bookkeeping for available expressions, leaders, or operand sets rather than a front-end parsing issue.

The option combination is crucial: `-O3` enables PRE, while `-fno-tree-dce -fno-tree-dse -fno-expensive-optimizations -fno-ssa-phiopt` disables passes that would normally simplify the CFG/SSA graph or remove dead statements before PRE runs. That leaves PRE seeing an unusual but valid intermediate form it does not handle correctly.

The report notes the source is valid C and that GCC 14.3 does not ICE, so this is a regression in optimizer robustness. The reproducer exercises a corner case where dead pure computations, mixed boolean/bitwise arithmetic, loop-carried SSA names, and PRE insertion interact badly on x86_64 at higher optimization levels.

A correct compiler behavior would be to accept the program, possibly optimize the unreachable loop away entirely because `a` is known zero in this translation unit, or at least preserve semantics without crashing. The observed internal compiler error is therefore strictly a compiler bug, not undefined behavior in the source.

Even if constant propagation can infer that `while (a)` is never entered, the disabled optimization mix may delay or prevent that simplification, allowing PRE to inspect expressions inside the loop. The reproducer thus relies on optimization pipeline ordering as much as on the source expression itself.

The discarded `~(c << 1);` and the complex assignment together are likely important because they create expression nodes involving shifts, complements, multiplies, booleanization, and reused names (`c`/`g`) that PRE may try to value-number or rebuild. Removing seemingly irrelevant statements in this kind of testcase often avoids the ICE by changing PRE's internal expression set.

Overall, the reproducer exercises GCC's SSA-based partial redundancy elimination on a valid loop containing dead pure code, short-circuit control flow, and precedence-heavy integer expressions, and exposes a regression where PRE attempts to generate an expression from inconsistent bitmap state and segfaults instead of compiling the code.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: This reproducer is a valid C optimization stress test centered on a loop whose body combines dead side-effect-free computation, a conditional call, loop-carried state, and a precedence-sensitive expression that mixes boolean, arithmetic, and bitwise operators. Under `-O3` with several cleanup/simplification passes disabled, GCC's `tree-ssa-pre` pass still analyzes and tries to insert partially redundant expressions on CFG edges. During that insertion work, PRE reaches `find_or_generate_expression` and crashes in bitmap iteration, indicating broken internal bookkeeping for an expression/operand set rather than any source-language error. In short, the testcase exercises a PRE corner case introduced after GCC 14.3, and the failure is an optimizer regression causing an ICE on valid code.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern is a regression in the GIMPLE SSA Partial Redundancy Elimination pass, not a front-end or source-validity issue. The testcase is valid C, and the crash happens only under an unusual optimization mix where PRE still runs but several cleanup/simplification passes are disabled. Common trigger patterns are: a loop with conditional control flow, loop-carried SSA names (`f` from `c`), a dead side-effect-free computation (`~(c << 1);`) that survives because DCE/DSE are disabled, and a complex expression that mixes booleanization, bitwise operators, arithmetic, and reused values (`c` and `g`). PRE reaches `find_or_generate_expression`, then `create_expression_by_pieces`, then insertion on predecessor edges, and finally segfaults in `bmp_iter_set_init`, which strongly suggests invalid internal bitmap/set bookkeeping while reconstructing or searching for an expression. The most likely defect class is that PRE assumes some expression/leader/availability bitmap is initialized and consistent, but under this pass ordering one expression form is left with missing or stale operand/value metadata. Because GCC 14.3 did not ICE, the bug is likely a regression in PRE expression generation or edge insertion logic introduced after 14.x, especially for booleanized integer expressions or dead pure expressions preserved into PRE.
possible_causes: `tree-ssa-pre.cc` may build or query an uninitialized/null bitmap for an expression's value set or leader set inside `find_or_generate_expression`, causing `bmp_iter_set_init` to dereference invalid state during PRE insertion.

PRE's `create_expression_by_pieces` / `insert_into_preds_of_block` logic may mishandle complex expressions that combine bitwise OR with a final logical AND, losing the expected normalized boolean form and leaving inconsistent operand bookkeeping for reconstruction on predecessor edges.

A regression in PRE value-numbering for equivalent names (`c` and local copy `g`) inside loops may create a stale or mismatched expression record after CFG-sensitive insertion, so later bitmap iteration uses freed, absent, or wrong-set metadata.

Disabling `tree-dce`, `tree-dse`, `expensive-optimizations`, and `ssa-phiopt` may expose a missing PRE guard: the pass likely assumes dead pure statements or certain PHI/canonicalization cleanups already happened, but when they do not, PRE tries to materialize an unsupported expression shape and crashes instead of bailing out.

PRE may mishandle reconstruction of side-effect-free but unused computations that survive into optimization, incorrectly treating them as available/generatable expressions without allocating the associated operand availability bitmaps.

Loop/edge insertion code in PRE may incorrectly process booleanized integer expressions whose final result is only `0/1`, especially when the underlying operands come from mixed signed/unsigned arithmetic and short-circuit control flow, leading to corrupted expression-availability state.
evidence: The ICE occurs during GIMPLE pass `pre`, with stack `find_or_generate_expression -> create_expression_by_pieces -> insert_into_preds_of_block -> bmp_iter_set_init`, directly implicating PRE expression reconstruction and bitmap iteration.

The crash is a segmentation fault in `bitmap.h:542` (`bmp_iter_set_init`), which is consistent with PRE passing an invalid or uninitialized bitmap/set rather than encountering a semantic source-language problem.

The testcase shape matches PRE stress conditions: loop, conditional call, loop-carried SSA value, reused equivalent values (`c` and `g`), and a complex precedence-sensitive expression that must be value-numbered and possibly rebuilt on edges.
`~(c << 1);` is dead pure code that normally would disappear, but the bug requires `-fno-tree-dce -fno-tree-dse`, showing PRE is seeing unusual surviving statements and expression nodes.

The option mix disables simplifying/canonicalizing passes (`-fno-expensive-optimizations -fno-ssa-phiopt`) while keeping `-O3` PRE active, which is a strong sign that PRE has an invalid assumption about prior pipeline cleanup or canonical forms.

The report states GCC 14.3 does not ICE but 15.1 and trunk do, so the failure is a regression in optimizer robustness, most plausibly in `tree-ssa-pre.cc` bookkeeping or insertion logic rather than in parsing or lowering.

selected_files.reason: Directly implicated by the ICE backtrace: the crash occurs in `find_or_generate_expression`, reached via `create_expression_by_pieces`, `insert_into_preds_of_block`, and PRE `execute`. The testcase shape and option mix strongly suggest a PRE bookkeeping/regression bug around expression reconstruction or availability/leader bitmaps.

The immediate fault is in `bmp_iter_set_init` from `bitmap.h`, which means PRE is iterating a bad bitmap or malformed set. While likely triggered by PRE misuse, this header is still highly suspicious because the segfault manifests at bitmap iteration initialization.

`tree-ssa-pre` relies on SCCVN/GVN metadata for value numbering and expression identities. A regression that creates stale or inconsistent value sets for equivalent expressions like `c` and `g` could surface later as invalid PRE bitmap/set state during insertion.

If the failure is not just PRE passing an invalid bitmap pointer, it could come from bitmap allocation/lifetime corruption. Since the crash is in bitmap iteration and PRE uses many bitmap-backed sets, the bitmap implementation is a plausible secondary source.

PRE computes anticipatability/availability and insertion points using lazy code motion style bitmap dataflow. A bug in shared LCM-style placement logic or its bitmap assumptions could leave PRE with inconsistent insertion-state on predecessor edges.

The crash happens while PRE inserts expressions into predecessor blocks. If CFG edge manipulation or block/edge metadata is left inconsistent for this unusual loop and conditional structure, PRE insertion could later walk invalid predecessor state.

PRE insertion rebuilds and inserts GIMPLE on edges/predecessor blocks. If statement insertion or block attachment/update helpers mishandle the generated sequence for this corner case, PRE's subsequent bookkeeping may become inconsistent.

The reproducer stresses mixed boolean, bitwise, and arithmetic expressions that PRE may rebuild piecewise. Incorrect operand cache construction or update for generated statements could corrupt the SSA/PRE metadata consumed during expression generation.

PRE often canonicalizes or rebuilds expressions through GIMPLE folding while generating code by pieces. A regression in folding booleanized integer expressions could create an unsupported or mismatched expression form that later breaks PRE bookkeeping.

The testcase depends on tricky type/boolean conversions across signed and unsigned arithmetic feeding logical operators. If expression/type canonicalization for generated GIMPLE is wrong, PRE may index or query expression metadata inconsistently and trip bitmap iteration later.

Those methods have both STATIC and EXTERNAL set. 2) In WHOPR mode devirtualization might lead to reference to method that was partitioned elsehwere. In this case we have static VAR_DECL or FUNCTION_DECL that has no corresponding callgraph/varpool node declaring the body. 3) COMDAT functions referred by external vtables that we devirtualize only during final compilation stage. At this time we already decided that we will not output the function body and thus we can't reference the symbol directly.

gcc/gimple-expr.cc.summary: Return true if the conversion from INNER_TYPE to OUTER_TYPE is a useless type conversion, otherwise return false. This function implicitly defines the middle-end type system. With the notion of 'a < b' meaning that useless_type_conversion_p (a, b) holds and 'a > b' meaning that useless_type_conversion_p (b, a) holds, the following invariants shall be fulfilled: 1) useless_type_conversion_p is transitive. If a < b and b < c then a < c. 2) useless_type_conversion_p is not symmetric. From a < b does not follow a > b. 3) Types define the available set of operations applicable to values. A type conversion is useless if the operations for the target type is a subset of the operations for the source type. For example casts to void* are useless, casts from void* are not (void* can't be dereferenced or offsetted, but copied, hence its set of operations is a strict subset of that of all other data pointer types). Casts to const T* are useless (can't be written to), casts from const T* to T* are not.
